subject: Clarify invoicing & MSA responsibilities for reseller listing (CloudWave)
messages:
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@cloudwave.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurements@cloudwave.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace invoicing question before redlines

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick follow up from our finance team. They want to confirm how invoices will flow when Redwood lists through CloudWave: specifically whether CloudWave will be the billing party (we invoice CloudWave; CloudWave invoices the end-customer) or if Redwood invoices end-customers directly and CloudWave receives a settlement/commission.

Also asked if there are any pass-through taxes or marketplace processing fees that Redwood expects CloudWave to collect/ remit. We have a draft addendum but want to align on the MSA/Order Form language before our legal completes redlines.

Can you point me to the relevant clause or share a short diagram? If convenient, cc'ing Procurement here for visibility.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Smith
Head of Cloud Partnerships — CloudWave
attachments: Invoice-flow-ask.txt
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace invoicing question before redlines

Jordan —

Quick note to acknowledge, and thanks for surfacing this early. Short answers up front:
- Preferred flow: CloudWave invoices the customer (marketplace billing) and Redwood invoices CloudWave for the net revenue share/settlement.
- Redwood can accept direct-invoice models for select customers but that requires a change to the Order Form and tax-responsibility box.
- Pass-through taxes: we typically ask the marketplace to collect and remit VAT/GST on our behalf in regions where the marketplace is the deemed provider. For US domestic sales we usually remain the seller of record unless CloudWave requests to be the seller.

I'm attaching a simple diagram + our standard redline bullets to make it concrete (see attached). Karthik & Laura — can you review the attached addendum v3 and confirm whether the current redlines capture the CloudWave preference to be billing party and how that affects the MSA clause on "Seller of Record" and invoice timing?

Thanks,
Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
attachments: Invoice-Routing-Diagram.pdf; CloudWave_Marketplace_Addendum_v3.docx
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 14:33:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Marketplace invoicing question before redlines

Mina / Laura —

Reviewed addendum v3 and left inline comments in Redlines-msav3.docx. Key legal points to resolve before we sign:

1) Seller of Record / Billing party (MSA §2.1):
   - If CloudWave is billing the customer, we need an explicit clause that CloudWave will:
     * collect payments as agent/principal (specify which),
     * remit net settlements to Redwood within X days (we typically use 30).
   - If CloudWave remains agent, Redwood must retain ability to invoice directly for certain customers (enterprise or regulatory).

2) Taxes & Pass-through fees (Order Form schedule B):
   - Put a table that clarifies responsibility by region: US (Redwood seller of record unless requested), EU (marketplace often collects VAT), APAC (case-by-case).

3) Evidence & Audit rights (Procurement asks):
   - Procurement asked for transaction-level reporting and monthly settlement statements. Add "Settlement Report" requirement and a quarterly reconciliation right.

4) Invoicing / Payment terms alignment:
   - In the addendum we added a 45-day settlement net to account for marketplace processing delays; finance prefers 30. Recommend we negotiate to 30 with a 60-day cap for disputed items.

I'll mark the redlines with suggested language. Laura — can you confirm whether a 30-day net is acceptable operationally?

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Channel Partnerships
attachments: Redlines-msav3.docx
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Marketplace invoicing question before redlines

Agree with Karthik's notes. A couple operational clarifications from billing team:
- Settlement files: SFTP delivery or S3 with daily batch; file schema must include order id, invoice id, billing country, tax collected, gross amount, commission %, net due.
- Dispute window: 60 days to raise a settlement dispute followed by 90 days to finalize reconciliation.

If CloudWave insists on being seller of record, we must include a carve for data residency / audit trail: Redwood needs transaction-level detail for 3 years for tax audits.

I'll prepare a short redline excerpt to drop into the addendum that covers: seller of record statement, settlement schedule, and settlement reporting schema.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Billing & Revenue Ops
From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@cloudwave.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@cloudwave.com>, Procurement Team <procurements@cloudwave.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace invoicing question before redlines

Thanks team — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:
- CloudWave will act as the billing party (seller of record) for standard marketplace transactions; for enterprise customers we can support Redwood invoicing directly if requested.
- We can provide daily settlement files via S3 (we support the schema Laura outlined).
- On remittance timing: 30-day net is OK, but can we agree to a 45-day net for months with heavy processing volume to avoid negative cash timing? We can put a 'standard 30-day with up to 45-day variability' clause into the addendum.

We will review the redline excerpt you circulate and push our legal to accept the minimum transaction-level fields.

-Jordan
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@cloudwave.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Procurement Team <procurements@cloudwave.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace invoicing question before redlines

Jordan —

Thanks — that sounds workable. Next steps I propose, and please confirm by EOD Monday:
1) Redwood legal will insert a short clause in the addendum: "CloudWave will be seller of record for standard marketplace transactions; Redwood retains right to invoice directly for specified customers listed in Order Forms."
2) Laura will provide the settlement file schema snippet and required retention window (3 years) — she will attach that to the redline excerpt.
3) Karthik will ask our finance to accept "standard 30-day net; up to 45 days in peak months" language and provide fallback dispute timing.
4) CloudWave legal to accept redlines and push to DocuSign. We will share a DocuSign link when redlines are agreed.

Attaching the updated addendum excerpt for ease of review: CloudWave_Marketplace_Addendum_v3.docx.

If we can get confirmation on the four items by Monday, we'll aim to finalize with legal and route to DocuSign by Wed next week.

-Mina
Mina Haddad
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
